historical_reviews.deepseek: OS enumeration is useful corroboration but cannot prove BIOS visibility, firmware fields or physical slot labels.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly changes the unconditional classification and covers all four device classes.
historical_reviews.history: Sequence 514 is a different physical-row variant sharing the code and tests file checksum; it supplies no reusable conclusion for this BIOS inventory case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Requires row/variant identity plus a per-device mapping matrix; counts alone cannot bind a BIOS label to a CPU socket, DIMM slot, drive bay or PCIe slot.

original_test_intent: Verify that BIOS setup correctly displays identity, firmware version, quantity and physical/logical slot for every expected CPU, DIMM, storage device and PCIe card on the configured system.
original_method: Bind the row variant and system recipe, collect complete stable-ID OS/BMC inventory, use validated console/operator access to capture every relevant BIOS device page read-only, reconcile BIOS labels and hidden/controller-managed devices, and exit without saving.
manual_activity: Operator or validated remote-console package enters BIOS, captures all CPU/DIMM/HDD/PCIe information pages and slot labels, and exits without saving.
safety_requirements: Bind physical row 1435, not duplicate row 336
Use read-only BIOS navigation and OS queries
Do not infer slots from enumeration order
Do not truncate lspci or storage inventory
Never query/write raw storage as part of inventory
Stop on target/recipe ambiguity or unexpected setup prompt
Verify normal boot and unchanged inventory
agent_execution_scope: Verify row variant and system identity
Load recipe and physical slot maps
engineer_actions: Define authoritative firmware source per device class

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: lscpu, dmidecode, lsblk and lspci can corroborate inventory, but the command truncates PCI devices, lacks stable storage/slot identities and does not implement the mandatory BIOS UI observation. Insecure SSH handling is unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Collect complete stable-ID inventory, capture every BIOS CPU/DIMM/storage/PCIe page via validated console, map each label/version/count/slot to the recipe, record legitimate visibility differences, and exit without saving.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All four device classes, information/version/quantity/slot criteria, BIOS-menu path and 5/5-minute timing are preserved; inventory and mappings are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a per-device matrix keyed by socket/slot/bay/BDF with BIOS label/value, stable OS/BMC identity, firmware source, recipe expectation and comparison result.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Converts generic visual inspection into auditable cross-source identity and slot reconciliation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects missing devices, wrong slot labels, stale firmware, duplicate entries and valid controller-hidden topology.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BIOS and OS may expose different abstraction layers; only an approved mapping can distinguish legitimate aggregation from missing coverage.

project_override_considerations: This duplicate code is not the row-336 File checksum testcase. The private Type 41 script may help onboard-device data but cannot cover all CPU, DIMM, drive and add-in-card pages without review.
expected_evidence: Protected BIOS captures for all device classes
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Within physical row 1435 the purpose and criteria consistently target BIOS device inventory. The duplicate code is an identity hazard handled by row/variant binding, not a semantic conflict in this row.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Recipe, mappings and console access are finite packages. Unresolved stable identity or unsafe navigation after request would block execution.

review_improvement: Prevents the duplicate File checksum variant or partial OS counts from substituting for complete BIOS identity, firmware and slot coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: The same code maps to two unrelated rows, so code-only lookup demonstrably selects the wrong testcase; sheet, physical row, hash and variant are mandatory. For this row, BIOS may label devices by socket/slot while OS tools expose NUMA, BDF or controller namespaces. A stable crosswalk and UI capture are required, making the hybrid case REQUIRES.
